reason: Hunter Brown carries a 2.45 xERA over his last 3 with a 29.0 K% and faces a middling SFG lineup at 97 wRC+ vs RHP over their last 12, and Houston's bullpen (1.90 xERA over its last 12) is built to protect a lead. The market has this priced as a straight ML at -194; the runline at -113 pays the same conviction at a fraction of the cost because a Whisenhunt start rarely stays a one-run game.

At plus money the line undersells a high-strikeout arm against one of the most strikeout-prone lineups he'll see.

Against a BAL group that isn't a heavy-whiff lineup, the number of punchouts required to clear 4.5 is well beyond anything he's produced recently.

Even at his 27.8 K% he cannot accumulate seven strikeouts in the workload a rusty, un-stretched starter will be given. The market is pricing his stuff rather than his innings, and the innings cap is the whole story here.

He goes deep enough (5.7 IP/gs) to keep the game away from Seattle's shaky bullpen for most of the outing. A cold lineup against an arm that specifically neutralizes it should not clear 3.5, and the market is pricing this at plus money.

Against this exact lineup he has gone 7, 6, and 5 strikeouts across 3 meetings at a 3.18 ERA and 5.7 IP/gs, so the length and the whiffs are both established here. His outs line of 17.5 gives him the innings, and a number sitting a full strikeout below his recent and head-to-head average is the value even at this price.

Bibee has dominated Detroit at Comerica Park — a 0.86 ERA at 7.0 IP/gs across his last 3 here and a 1.71 ERA over his last 3 meetings overall, a consistent five-start pattern that outweighs Detroit's hot 146 wRC+ vs RHP. His counterpart Anderson has thrown just 6.1 IP over 3 starts and only 42 pitches last time, not stretched out and prone to a short leash that exposes an average Detroit bullpen early. Taking Cleveland through five at plus money sidesteps their weak relief corps and prices Bibee's ownership of this matchup correctly.

McLean has been steady against Atlanta across his last 3 meetings — 2ER, 2ER, and 2ER over 3.18 ERA and 5.7 IP/gs, with a 2.77 ERA over 2 starts in this park. The market has ATL as a home favorite on Perez's shiny ERA, but the actual matchup — McLean containing a 97-wRC+ Atlanta lineup while the Mets keep hitting Perez — makes a plus-money underdog the wrong price.

The market is discounting how quickly this outing unravels; five-plus Astros runs is the more likely outcome than the number implies.

Against San Diego across two prior meetings he averaged 4.5 IP, again short of this line. A pitcher on a consistently short leash priced at plus money to fall under his typical depth is mispriced.

St. Louis strikes out at just a 17.9% rate vs LHP over their last 12, and in two prior starts against them Sanchez averaged only 5.5 strikeouts per outing despite going a full six innings each time. His gaudy 30.3% K rate over his last 3 was built against strikeout-prone NYY and BAL lineups, so it overstates what he gets tonight. Plus money on the under against a contact-oriented lineup he has historically not piled up strikeouts against is value.
